answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes, once the operator knows or should know that the accident has occurred. A death of an individual at the mine is one of the listed accidents.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes once the operator knows or should know an accident has occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is an accident covered by this notification requirement.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where methane is not present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent (with an increase of 0.4 percent per 0.1 percent methane only where methane is present).
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: Each underground coal miner (and authorized visitors) must be given an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect that person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: The operator must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift, at a time other than a shift change, and involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. Section 48.5 covers this. Approximately 8 of those hours are given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 hours of the training is given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA. That is equivalent to a dose of 100% of what the standard permits.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This requirement appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway (56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same height requirement appears in 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. The Emergency Response Plan rules allow 48 hours only if advance arrangements are made to get additional supplies to anyone who can't be rescued within that time.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

claims.text: A refuge alternative that sustains persons for only 48 hours requires the ERP to detail advance arrangements for additional supplies for anyone who cannot be rescued within 48 hours.
claims.quote: If the refuge alternative sustains persons for only 48 hours, the ERP shall detail advanced arrangements that have been made to assure that persons who cannot be rescued within 48 hours will receive additional supplies to sustain them until rescue.

answers.question: What must a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan contain under OSHA?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say what a written bloodborne pathogens exposure control plan must contain under OSHA. They cover MSHA respiratory protection programs, training plan implementation, and airborne contaminants. None of them mention bloodborne pathogens.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The chunks don't say. They cover mining regulations (30 CFR), such as shaft bucket requirements and protective clothing. They contain nothing on OSHA construction trench depth requirements or protective systems like shoring or trench boxes.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design plans, permits for mining under water, and exemptions. None of them mention EPA stormwater discharge permits.
